_about: Tables for world/ECOLOGY.md. Stocks follow a Schaefer surplus-production model (logistic growth minus catch); parameters are illustrative per species class and a belt data task. Historical depletion from the Cayman turtle fishery and Barbados soil. mark: rex | proposed | open.

stocks.title: Fish, turtle and game stocks (Schaefer model parameters, per local ground)
stocks.source: Schaefer 1954 surplus production: B(t+1) = B + r B (1 - B/K) - C; MSY = rK/4 at B = K/2 (FAO; ECO-SCHAEFER). r values are the keeper's reading of life history (fast for small pelagics, slow for turtles and sharks); K is per fishing ground in units of catch-days. Turtle depletion: the Cayman fishery was already in decline when permanent settlers arrived in the early 1700s; 1,200 to 1,400 turtles a year sold at Jamaica in 1787; the fleet moved to the Miskito Cays by the early 1800s (ECO-TURTLE). Fish species named are those period sailors caught from the rail (DUTIES.md: dolphin fish, bonito, shark, flying fish; FISHING.md).

depletion_rules.title: Depletion and regeneration rules
depletion_rules.source: Logistic recovery is the Schaefer model's own; the catch-per-effort fall is the standard signal (CPUE proportional to B); the 'tragedy' row is the Cayman history. The fishing minigame's catch (FISHING.md stage 1, reading the water) is the visible face: fewer silhouettes.

crops.title: Crops: yields, seasons and soil
crops.source: Ligon 1657 on Barbados cane (planted in rows, 14 to 16 months to ripen; replanted from cuttings; cassava and potatoes as bread; plantains); modern tropical agronomy for cycle lengths; Barbados deforested and its soil exhausted within decades of 1640, with heavy manuring and cane-holing the response (ECO-SOIL). Yields are modern unimproved-tropical figures, not period measurements.

soil.title: Soil fertility model
soil.source: A fertility index per field (0 to 1) drained by each crop's demand and restored by manure, fallow and legumes; Barbados exhaustion and the planters' manuring response are the historical anchor (ECO-SOIL). Numbers are placeholders.

seasons.title: The year's calendar for the world tick
seasons.source: Dry season December to May, wet June to November; hurricane season June to November peaking August to October; turtle nesting May to September; the Spanish fleets sailed from Havana in spring and summer to avoid the hurricane months (period practice); sugar crop cut January to May in the dry season (Ligon).
